flashcard_questions.q: How long should hands be washed before handling food?
Why are blue plasters used in food preparation areas?
flashcard_questions.a: No natural food is blue, so a fallen plaster is easy to spot.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the 48-hour rule for food handlers?
flashcard_questions.a: Wait 48 hours after vomiting or diarrhoea stops before preparing food for others.

flashcard_questions.q: Which colour chopping board is used for raw meat?
What temperature range should a refrigerator be kept at?
What temperature should a freezer operate at?
Why does freezing not make contaminated food safe?
flashcard_questions.a: Freezing only stops bacteria multiplying; it does not kill them.

flashcard_questions.q: What does FIFO stand for in dry storage?
What core temperature and time make cooked food safe?
At what minimum temperature must hot food be held on a buffet?
How many times may food safely be reheated?
What is the only reliable way to check a safe core temperature?
What does a use-by date tell you?
flashcard_questions.a: It is a safety date; the food must not be eaten after it.

flashcard_questions.q: What does a best-before date tell you?
flashcard_questions.a: It is a quality date; food is still safe afterwards but may be past its best.

flashcard_questions.q: Which date marking is used only by shops for stock control?

notes: 15 cards: 6 value cards (20 seconds, fridge 0-5°C, freezer -18°C, 75°C for 2 minutes, 63°C hot holding, reheat once), 4 process/rule cards, 3 date-marking cards, 2 practice cards. Kept only one chopping-board colour card because the full six-colour set would interfere card against card, and dropped the board list, the personal-hygiene bullet list and the 2.4 million illness figure. Cooling within 90 minutes is left to the spoilage lesson.
